assessment: This important study shows that the expression of some inhibitory receptors on CD8 T cells is increased in people living with HIV (PLWH) and remains elevated even after years of viral suppression by antiretroviral therapy. The authors further provide convincing evidence that inhibition of TGIT partially restores the ability of CD8 T cells to produce CD107a but not the other functions and is relevant for researchers and clinicians interested in viral infections, especially HIV/AIDS.
